1	/**
2	 * Regenerates `public/previews/<host>.jpg`, one per project in `content.json`.
3	 *
4	 * Every preview is a static screenshot: the live iframes pulled 40-50 third-party
5	 * requests into the page and cost the Lighthouse budget of spec 17 (Performance 0.82,
6	 * Best Practices 0.79 on `/en`). Run this by hand when a client site is redesigned:
7	 *
8	 *     bun scripts/capture-previews.ts [host ...]
9	 *
10	 * Playwright is already the dev dependency of the E2E suite, so this adds nothing.
11	 */
12	import { chromium } from '@playwright/test'
13	
14	import { content } from '../src/lib/content'
15	
16	// 16:11, the aspect ratio of the card's `.preview` box. The page lays out at 1440 CSS
17	// pixels — a desktop, not a squeezed phone — and is written out at two thirds of that,
18	// which is still ~2.7x the ~360px the card is ever painted at and a third of the bytes.
19	const VIEWPORT = { width: 1440, height: 990 }
20	const SCALE = 2 / 3
21	
22	// Cookie walls make for a useless preview, so the first matching control gets clicked.
23	// Spanish and English, the two languages these sites ship in.
24	const CONSENT =
25	  /^(accept|accept all|allow all|got it|ok|agree|i agree)|(acept|entend|de acuerdo|permitir)/i
26	
27	const hosts = new Set(content.es.projects.map((project) => project.host))
28	const only = process.argv.slice(2)
29	
30	const browser = await chromium.launch()
31	const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: VIEWPORT, deviceScaleFactor: SCALE })
32	
33	for (const project of content.es.projects) {
34	  if (only.length > 0 && !only.includes(project.host)) continue
35	  if (!hosts.delete(project.host)) continue
36	
37	  console.log(`→ ${project.host}`)
38	  await page.goto(project.url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 60_000 })
39	  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle', { timeout: 30_000 }).catch(() => {})
40	
41	  for (const button of await page.getByRole('button').all()) {
42	    const label = (await button.textContent().catch(() => ''))?.trim() ?? ''
43	    if (!CONSENT.test(label)) continue
44	    await button.click({ timeout: 5_000 }).catch(() => {})
45	    break
46	  }
47	
48	  // Entrance animations are the norm on these sites; a screenshot taken mid-fade is a
49	  // screenshot of nothing.
50	  await page.waitForTimeout(4_000)
51	  // JPEG, not PNG: these are photographic screenshots, where PNG cost 2.5 MB across the
52	  // six against 723 KB here for the same 960x660 pixels.
53	  await page.screenshot({ path: `public/previews/${project.host}.jpg`, quality: 82 })
54	}
55	
56	await browser.close()

1	// How each project is previewed. Declarative and keyed by **host**, never by position
2	// in `content.json`: reordering the list must not put a live iframe on a site that
3	// answers `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, which is exactly what an index-keyed table would do.
4	// Header check run on 2026-09-05 (design doc §8).
5	
6	export type PreviewMode = 'iframe' | 'screenshot'
7	
8	export const PREVIEWS: Record<string, PreviewMode> = {
9	  'nera-agro.com': 'iframe',
10	  'agropro.ag': 'iframe',
11	  'kodaiverse.com': 'iframe',
12	  'masushuaia.com': 'iframe',
13	  // `X-Frame-Options: DENY` + `frame-ancestors 'none'`.
14	  'creativamedialab.com': 'screenshot',
15	  // Does not answer `curl` at all (WAF).
16	  'telecentro.com.ar': 'screenshot',
17	}
18	
19	/**
20	 * A host nobody declared falls back to a screenshot: an undeclared site may well refuse
21	 * to be framed, and a placeholder is a far cheaper mistake than an empty iframe. The
22	 * unit test is what keeps a new project in `content.json` from staying undeclared.
23	 */
24	export function previewMode(host: string): PreviewMode {
25	  return PREVIEWS[host] ?? 'screenshot'
26	}
27	
28	/**
29	 * Reveal stagger of the projects grid (`MOTION_SPEC` §9): 90ms per column, restarting
30	 * on every row, so a card is never held back by the rows above it. Three columns is the
31	 * widest the grid ever gets at `minmax(min(100%, 300px), 1fr)` inside `container-page`.
32	 */
33	export function projectDelay(index: number): number {
34	  return 90 * (index % 3)
35	}

32	/**
33	 * Every declaration of the built CSS with the stack of at-rules that encloses it.
34	 * Minified CSS is one line, so this walks braces instead of matching a shape.
35	 */
36	function declarations(styles: string) {
37	  const found: { declaration: string; selector: string; enclosing: string[] }[] = []
38	  const stack: string[] = []
39	  let buffer = ''
40	
41	  const flush = () => {
42	    const declaration = buffer.trim()
43	    buffer = ''
44	    if (!declaration.includes(':')) return
45	    const selector = stack.at(-1) ?? ''
46	    found.push({ declaration, selector, enclosing: [...stack] })
47	  }
48	
49	  for (const char of styles) {
50	    if (char === '{') {
51	      stack.push(buffer.trim())
52	      buffer = ''
53	    } else if (char === '}') {
54	      flush()
55	      stack.pop()
56	    } else if (char === ';') {
57	      flush()
58	    } else {
59	      buffer += char
60	    }
61	  }
62	  return found
63	}

content.text: Now I have enough context to assess. Let me review my analysis: **Files reviewed:** 1. `scripts/capture-previews.ts` — new dev/build script (manually run) that uses Playwright to visit `project.url` from `content.json` and writes screenshots to `public/previews/${project.host}.jpg`. 2. `src/lib/projects.ts` — narrows `PreviewMode` to `'screenshot'` only, removing all `iframe` modes. 3. `tests/a11y.test.ts` — drops the `frames.length > 0` floor now that no iframes are emitted; the per-iframe a11y assertions still fire if any iframe is reintroduced. 4. `tests/projects.test.ts` — replaces iframe-related assertions with screenshot-existence checks. **Data flow trace:** - `project.host` and `project.url` in `capture-previews.ts` come from `handoff/content.json` (via `src/lib/content.ts`), which is repo-controlled content, not a network / user-supplied source. Any path-traversal in `${project.host}.jpg` or SSRF-shaped concern via `page.goto(project.url)` would require an attacker to land a malicious PR — reviewer-gated, dev-only script, not a runtime sink. - The consent regex `/^(accept|...)|(acept|entend|de acuerdo|permitir)/i` has an unanchored second alternation (missing `^` inside the second group), so it can match substrings mid-label ("I do not accept"). This is a correctness/UX bug for a dev screenshot script; there is no security impact — the worst case is a bad screenshot on the maintainer's machine. - Net posture change is a **reduction** of attack surface: four live cross-origin iframes are being replaced with static images. The `` sink in `Projects.astro` receives `/previews/${project.host}.` — still trusted content. - The a11y test's removed floor assertion (`frames.length > 0`) is compensated by the new "no iframe survives" assertion in `projects.test.ts` and by the per-iframe checks still running unconditionally. - No new HTTP handlers, no auth/policy changes, no SQL/shell/eval sinks, no telemetry-of-secrets patterns, no allowlist/permission changes touching production code paths. No security vulnerabilities found that meet the reporting bar. (There is a functional mismatch — `Projects.astro` still checks for `.png` while the capture script and tests use `.jpg` — but that is a correctness bug, not a security issue, and outside the scope of this review.)
